capture.note: Telemetry signals are compacted for deterministic replay and enriched with deploy and commit records.

incident.title: Checkout failures delay payment processing
incident.summary: Checkout errors rose after a deployment. Payment calls fail, retries grow, and accounting and fraud consumers fall behind.

evidence.title: Checkout error rate
evidence.fact: Error rate rose from 0.7% to 38.4% within one minute of checkout deployment deploy-checkout-442.

evidence.title: Consumer lag
evidence.fact: orders.v1 consumer lag climbed from 182 to 11842 after checkout retries accelerated.

evidence.title: Accounting consumer delay
evidence.fact: Accounting logged processing_delay_ms=183000 for orders.v1 partition 3.

evidence.title: Kafka broker health
evidence.fact: All brokers remained available with zero under-replicated partitions and normal produce latency.

evidence.title: Failure ordering
evidence.fact: Payment connection failures began 171 seconds before Kafka lag crossed the alert threshold.

evidence.title: Checkout deployment
evidence.fact: deploy-checkout-442 promoted checkout:2.18.0 from commit c7e1b9a. The previous image was checkout:2.17.3.

evidence.title: Payment span failure
evidence.fact: Trace 4f91 shows checkout calling payment:9090. The span ends with ECONNREFUSED before any Kafka publish span begins.

evidence.title: Checkout endpoint selection
evidence.fact: checkout:2.18.0 logged PAYMENT_ADDR missing; using fallback payment:9090. The deployment supplies PAYMENT_SERVICE_ADDR=payment:8080.

evidence.title: AI-assisted timeout hardening
evidence.fact: Commit c7e1b9a changed endpoint lookup from PAYMENT_SERVICE_ADDR to PAYMENT_ADDR with fallback payment:9090. Deployment configuration was not updated.

value.provenance: AI-generated change accepted during checkout timeout hardening

evidence.title: Payment reachability restored
evidence.fact: After rollback to checkout:2.17.3, payment reachability returned to 99.98% and ECONNREFUSED stopped.

evidence.title: Checkout recovered
evidence.fact: Checkout error rate fell from 38.4% to 0.8% within two minutes of rollback.

evidence.title: Kafka backlog draining
evidence.fact: Consumer lag fell from 11842 to 620 and continued decreasing without any Kafka repair.

repair.abort_if: checkout ready replicas below 2 for more than 30 seconds

regression.name: Reject downstream Kafka blame when payment failures lead lag
regression.must_reject_hypothesis: Kafka broker degradation initiated the incident.
